veranderings.rede: Used attributively before a noun, the adjective takes the inflected form 'vroeëre'; 'vroeër farao's is' reads as a broken adverb construction.
Attributive adjective needs the inflected form 'latere', as the glossary entry for Vallei van die Konings already writes it.

veranderings.voor: naby Thebe verder suid langs die Nyl
veranderings.na: naby Thebe, verder suid langs die Nyl
veranderings.rede: A comma shows that 'verder suid langs die Nyl' describes the valley's position relative to Giza, not a place south of Thebe.

veranderings.voor: die Konings naby Thebe verder suid.
veranderings.na: die Konings naby Thebe, verder suid.
veranderings.rede: Same clarifying comma as in the study block, so 'verder suid' attaches to the valley and not to Thebe.
Natural Afrikaans word order is 'nog niemand'; 'niemand nog' sounds translated.
A single step is a 'trede'; 'trap' means the whole staircase, so 'die eerste trap van 'n kliptrap' is confusing and repetitive.

veranderings.voor: het Carter die eerste keer binne gekyk
veranderings.na: het Carter vir die eerste keer na binne gekyk
veranderings.rede: The idiomatic forms are 'vir die eerste keer' and 'na binne kyk'; 'binne gekyk' on its own reads unidiomatically.

veranderings.voor: het die ingang bedek en versteek
veranderings.na: het die klein graf se ingang bedek en versteek
veranderings.rede: The previous sentence names two graves, so 'die ingang' is ambiguous; naming the small grave makes clear whose entrance was hidden.
In written Afrikaans the subordinating conjunction is 'totdat'; 'tot' as a conjunction is colloquial.
'Ruim' is an uncommon word for a Grade 5 reader; 'meer as' says the same thing plainly.
